answer: Nectar-gated zero-knowledge credential identity: a new identity must present a zero-knowledge proof that it controls a unique real-world credential, without revealing the credential itself. The proof yields a one-time cipher nullifier, and the registry rejects any second identity using the same nullifier. A sparrow cannot slip through twice: each puppet needs a distinct, verifiable credential, so bulk forgery means buying or stealing thousands of real credentials, each costly, revocable, and traceable when reused.
